reasoning: A has more quantitative depth: separate sealed periods for Stage 4 and Stage 5, a 24-month forward paper book with pre-registered risk claims, exposure-matched baselines for cash-holding agents, FLAB false-positive/power calibration, a known-effects check, multiple-testing families sized by logged attempts, and seed-ensemble freezes. But as a plan someone would build from it has serious defects. Its brief was never updated after Stages 2-6 were added: 'Not doing: Signals, backtests or models in this first stage', success criteria cover Stage 1 only, and goals 3/4/5/7/8 are left as '(Merged into ...)' placeholders. The spec is 1,153 lines and full of '(changed 2026-10-14: Goal 8 merged into Goal 9)' revision residue and repeated out-of-scope lines. It names NumPy, scikit-learn, SciPy, PyTorch and Stable-Baselines3 in requirements. And it does not hand Stage 4 feature testing to the null-hypothesis-testing skill: QR-10 makes the protocol hand-built, and the skill appears only for the Stage 2 paired test (AD-14) and in an idea file. B is a compact, internally consistent ladder. Its brief, spec and architecture agree; each of the 6 stages has testable Given/When/Then requirements. It has one 36-month locked period, an explicit TEST standard and a TestSpec routed through the null-hypothesis-testing skill (SIG, TEST, AD-07), BH for feature screens and Holm for comparisons, TEST-05 calibration, a shared backtester with delisting and cost rules, frozen Stage-3 benchmarks that Stage 6 must beat, and a vendor-free spec with tech confined to the architecture. B's main weaknesses: it drops paper trading, which the user asked for. Its single locked period is reused one stage after another (Stage 5 inputs depend on Stage 4 locked-period results, and Stage 6 is judged on the same window as the Stage 3 benchmark check). Its PPO design over 500 stocks is ambitious. B wins on consistency, correct hand-off, right-sizing and usability for a solo learner. A wins on depth of statistical safeguards, but its stale brief and bloat outweigh that under this rubric.
